question.text: Which of the following correctly describes the Sensex and Nifty 50?

answer.text: Sensex comprises 30 stocks with base year 1978-79 (value 100), while Nifty 50 comprises 50 stocks with base date November 3, 1995 (value 1000)
Sensex comprises 50 stocks with base year 1995 (value 1000), while Nifty 50 comprises 30 stocks with base year 1978-79 (value 100)
Both Sensex and Nifty 50 comprise 50 stocks each with the same base year of 2000
Sensex comprises 30 stocks with base value 1000, while Nifty 50 comprises 50 stocks with base value 100

explanation.text: The Logic: The Sensex (BSE Sensitive Index) is BSE's flagship benchmark made up of 30 large component stocks, computed with a base year of 1978-79 and a base value of 100. The Nifty 50 is NSE's flagship benchmark made up of 50 component stocks, with a base date of November 3, 1995 and a base value of 1,000. Both indices today are calculated on a free-float market-capitalization methodology and are used as the reference benchmarks for index funds and index derivatives. The Trap: The second option reverses the number of stocks and base settings between the two indices. The third option incorrectly says both have 50 stocks and a shared base year of 2000. The fourth option swaps the base values - Sensex's base is 100 and Nifty's is 1,000, not the other way around. Note: The exact base-year/base-value facts (1978-79=100 for Sensex; Nov 3, 1995=1,000 for Nifty) are not stated on the cited pages of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives workbook; the source on the pages checked supports Sensex and Nifty as popular Indian indices using free-float methodology with 30/50 component companies. The specific base-date and base-value figures above are general index-construction facts.
